label: <DEL> step in long (L>=8) sequences
explanation: Low end of candidate unit 44 fires mainly on the <DEL> step (67% of mass at the delimiter). Delimiter firing rate depends strongly on sequence length: about 0 for L<=6, low for L=7, high for L=8 and L=9. The predicate <DEL> & L>=8 has precision ~0.87 and holds ~62% of mass. It covers the top activations best (80% of the top quartile), and the largest values are at <DEL> in L=8/9 sequences. Weaker activations spill onto the last original token (to_go=0, L=9) and the first copy output. There is also a diffuse copy-phase tail (~24% of mass) that is enriched for inputs z, g, o, t and rises toward the end of long sequences; I found no clean rule for it. Never fires at t<=5 or on early original positions.
